dashboard_live_view: Live view of the saved evaluation results — {generator}
dashboard_answer_quality: Answer quality by language and mode
dashboard_answer_quality_desc: Judge correctness (0–5), primary generator. n per cell shown in parentheses. Failures are answers scoring ≤ 3 on the judge scale: 0 = refusal/no answer, 1 = completely wrong, 2 = mostly wrong, 3 = partially correct; 4 = mostly correct with minor omissions, 5 = fully correct.
comparison_subtitle: Per-language quality waterfall from the saved evaluation — {generator}
comparison_note: Reading/generation gap = gold-context drop vs English · retrieval gap = RAG drop vs gold context · input gap = Romanized-query drop vs native-script RAG. All values are judge correctness (0–5).
failure_subtitle: Real failure records from the saved evaluation (correctness ≤ 3) — {generator}
failure_no_matches: No failures match the current filters.
failure_matching_failures: matching failures shown (sorted by lowest correctness first)
about_subtitle: Where does answer quality drop in Indian-language chatbots?
about_what_is_desc: BhashaCore evaluates a RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) chatbot pipeline across {en} (control) and five Indic languages — {hi}, {ta}, {te}, {kn}, {ml} — decomposing answer quality into:
about_knowledge_desc: closed-book QA (what the model already knows)
about_retrieval_desc: end-to-end RAG over a BM25 retrieval pool
about_input_normalization_desc: Romanized ("Hinglish") queries through the same RAG
about_qa_data: QA data: AI4Bharat IndicQA (Indic languages) and SQuAD v1.1 validation (English control)
about_retrieval_pools: Retrieval pools: all QA contexts for the language + ~3,000 distractor passages from IndicCorp v2 (English distractors from SQuAD train)
about_judge: Judge: meta/muse-glimmer-30b — a different model family, translate-then-judge in English
about_judge_correctness_desc: LLM-judged answer correctness against the dataset's gold answers, scored after silent translation to English. Scale: 0 = refusal/no answer, 1 = completely wrong, 2 = mostly wrong, 3 = partially correct, 4 = mostly correct with minor omissions, 5 = fully correct. An answer counts as a failure when it scores ≤ 3 — this is the threshold behind the 530-failure figure on the dashboard.
about_faithfulness_desc: How well the answer is supported by the context passages actually provided to the model
about_em_f1_desc: Script-aware extractive scores (NFC normalization, punctuation/format-char stripping)
about_script_purity_desc: Fraction of alphabetic characters in the expected Unicode block of the response language
about_recall_mrr_desc: Whether the gold passage is in the top-5 retrieved, and its reciprocal rank (BM25 retrieval)
about_chat_bm25: The chat performs real BM25 retrieval over the indexed research corpus for the selected language and attaches the retrieved passages as citations.
about_chat_grounded: When the retrieved passages contain sufficient evidence for a known evaluation question, an answer is generated and the used passages are cited.
about_chat_refusal: When the corpus does not contain sufficient evidence, the assistant refuses to answer and attaches the closest low-confidence matches as references (clearly marked "not used").
about_chat_citations: Citations always refer to real retrieved passages with their passage IDs, sources, and retrieval scores.
about_dataset_gold_desc: no LLM API key is configured on this machine, so grounded answers come from the evaluation dataset's own gold answers (labelled dataset-eval-gold), not from a live language model. Configure NVIDIA_API_KEY to enable live generation through the NVIDIA NIM endpoint — retrieval, citations, and evidence checks are identical either way.
about_limit_independent_samples: Independent (not question-paired) samples per language; n = 50 questions per language per mode (achieved n reported in the summary CSV).
about_limit_bm25: BM25-only retrieval reflects a common low-cost deployment, not the best achievable pipeline.
about_limit_romanized: Romanized-query stress uses ITRANS transliteration, which is cleaner than real user input.
about_limit_judge: LLM-as-judge scores come from one judge model; judge bias cannot be fully eliminated.
about_limit_distractors: English distractors come from SQuAD train while Indic distractors come from IndicCorp v2 — noise profiles differ slightly.
about_limit_not_guidance: Answers are research-corpus demonstrations, not verified government guidance.
